properties.decision:
OPTIONS
(a) ONE FILE PER NODE AND ONE FILE PER EDGE. ⭐ RECOMMENDED. Nodes go under docs/design/<project>/nodes/<Type>/<escaped-id>.json. Edges go under docs/design/<project>/edges/<2-char fan-out>/<stable hash of type+from+to>.json. A small stamp file (schema version, graph_id) changes only on a schema bump. Every file is canonical JSON with sorted keys, so a byte difference always means a content difference. Two branches conflict only when they change the SAME node or the SAME edge differently, which is a real conflict and appears as one.
(b) ONE FILE PER NODE, CARRYING ITS OUTGOING EDGES as a sorted list, one per line. Fewer files (~5k not ~37k for reflow2), but git conflicts when two branches add edges at adjacent sorted positions from the same node. That is common for hub nodes, and it is a false conflict.
(c) KEEP ONE FILE AND MOVE ONLY THE CHAIN OUT. This removes the guaranteed header conflict, but a 21 MB single document still conflicts textually whenever two branches edit nearby nodes, and GitHub shows it as unreadable.
RECOMMENDED (a). Measured sizes for reflow2 today: 5,303 nodes and ~32,400 edges, so ~38k small files. git handles that routinely; a clone and checkout cost more files but no more bytes. Deletion is `git rm` of one file, and a rename is an add plus a delete. The custom merge driver becomes unnecessary for correctness. It is kept only as an optional semantic-conflict explainer.
MIGRATION: `export_graph` writes the new layout and `import_graph` reads both. reflow2_init converts a consumer on update. A one-release window reads the old single file and writes the new layout, and the gate accepts either during that window. The old-layout reader is removed a release later.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-03 — the committed design is laid out one file per node and one per edge, so git's ordinary merge merges it
properties.rationale: Designed 2026-09-23 on Anthony's instruction, for req:the-saved-design-merges-correctly-under-gits-ordinary-merge. PROPOSED for his word. (b) was rejected on its own measured risk: in reflow2's graph the most-connected nodes carry hundreds of edges, and those are exactly where two branches both add edges. The file count in (a) is the price of never having a false conflict, and the requirement asks for "disjoint changes never conflict", which only (a) guarantees. The canonical sorted writer matters for another reason too: fact:the-merge-driver-writes-the-merged-export-in-a-different-byte-layout-than-the-exporter-2026-09-22 showed that two writers with different layouts turn a 115-line change into a 380,000-line diff.
